summary: This work isolates two-level system (TLS) microwave losses in commercial niobium oxide powders by measuring their quality factors in a 3D superconducting cavity. The authors find that monoclinic Nb$_2$O$_5$ exhibits clear TLS-dominated losses consistent with the tunneling model, while tetragonal NbO$_2$ shows negligible TLS signatures, suggesting oxide phase and crystal symmetry are critical factors in determining TLS loss in niobium resonators.
motivation: TLS losses in amorphous oxides limit the performance of superconducting qubits and cavities, but the relative contributions from different niobium oxide phases in the native oxide stack remain unclear. Direct experimental comparison of isolated oxide phases is needed to identify which phases dominate dissipation.
method: Commercially obtained microcrystalline Nb$_2$O$_5$ (monoclinic, XRD-confirmed) and NbO$_2$ (tetragonal) powders (~20 mg each, 99.9% purity) were deposited on sapphire substrates using nail polish binder and inserted into a Nb cavity at the electric field antinode. Quality factors were measured via transmission ($S_{21}$) fitting versus circulating power ($P_\mathrm{circ}$ from $-75$ to $+35$ dBm) and temperature (60 mK to 1.1 K) using a vector network analyzer.
result: Nb$_2$O$_5$ samples show power-dependent $Q_i$ reduction with fits to Eq. 2 yielding small $\beta \approx 0.1$--0.3 (indicating TLS-TLS interactions), loss tangent $\delta = (8.1 \pm)\times10^{-4}$ to $1.8\times10^{-3}$ (Methods I and II), and $Q_i$ increasing ~10× from 60 mK to 1.1 K; NbO$_2$ samples show flat $Q_i$ across power, with dissipation only at high power consistent with quasiparticle effects, establishing monoclinic Nb$_2$O$_5$ as the primary TLS source in the Nb oxide stack.
